tasks.short: Answer calls, provide information, connect callers, take messages and pass appointment requests.

steps.what: Answer the call and establish the caller's purpose and urgency.
Find the relevant employee, department or published information.
Give an answer where approved information covers the question.

loop.input: Receptionist-entered question and approved, disclosure-filtered answer references.
loop.output: Short suggested answer with supporting references.
loop.check: Require a reference for each factual claim. The receptionist checks relevance before speaking.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction maximum. Missing support or ambiguity returns the question to the receptionist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact lookup handles fixed questions; varied wording sometimes needs a short synthesis.

steps.what: Check the recipient and transfer calls requiring another employee.
Write and send a callback message when the recipient is unavailable.

loop.input: Receptionist notes, confirmed callback details and selected recipient.
loop.check: Preserve confirmed names and numbers exactly. Require recipient and callback details before sending.
loop.stop: One draft maximum. Incomplete details return to the receptionist; structured notes bypass the model.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template covers structured messages; free notes sometimes need concise rewriting.

steps.what: Pass appointment requirements into the booking process.

tasks.design: Configure directory lookup and approved routing in the {TELEPHONY}, using a restricted directory from the {HCM} and information from the {DOCS}. A small panel in the {WORKFLOW} offers referenced answer drafts and callback messages for receptionist approval, then passes booking requirements to the {CALENDAR}. Calls continue with a person; no call recording is required.
tasks.previous_blocker: Basic routing already existed. Stale directories, scattered information and repeated message entry left much of the work manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing routing features and interfaces can handle the structured work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building a small connecting panel; bounded drafting handles variable wording.
tasks.still_hard: Identifying distressed callers, detecting misleading requests and finding the right person when responsibilities overlap.
tasks.human_edge: The receptionist hears urgency, builds trust and decides when a caller needs personal attention.

ambition.what: A tracked callback service for callers who cannot reach the right employee.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to searching and typing. The receptionist can prioritise unresolved callbacks within agreed service rules; disclosure and escalation limits still apply.

reach.task: Manage overflow routing during busy periods.
reach.learn: Queue settings, availability states and transfer failure handling.

reach.task: Follow up unresolved information requests.
reach.learn: Case ownership, response commitments and clear handover notes.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-based answers with handover are available today; this supports the answer-panel component.
Voice and other customer-service integrations are available today; local routing still needs validation.
Human support assistants have improved issue throughput in a documented study; reception gains cannot be inferred directly.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The baseline is a staffed reception desk using the {TELEPHONY}, a staff directory and internal messages.
Answering, transfer, message-taking and booking handoff are alternative call branches; shares cover the overall task mix.
The {HCM} exposes only reception-approved directory fields.
Booking execution is covered in task 43-4171.00:751; its savings must not be counted again here.
GDPR applies to caller details. Access and retention are limited to the callback purpose.
If caller-facing AI is later introduced, EU AI Act disclosure requirements apply; that extension is outside this design.
Consultation requirements depend on national rules and any change to employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which routing and directory features are already licensed?
Which questions reception may answer and which staff details it may disclose.
Actual call branches, volumes, languages and transfer failures.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
Who may prioritise callbacks and who must close them.
research_questions: Can the {TELEPHONY} expose directory lookup and approved transfers without custom call control?
Can supported answers be retrieved accurately without recording or transcribing calls?
new_work: Review suggested answers and callback messages.
Maintain directory mappings and approved answer references.
Handle failed transfers and overdue callbacks.
Check access logs and delete expired callback details.
tasks.statement: Operate telephone switchboard to answer, screen, or forward calls, providing information, taking messages, or scheduling appointments.

tasks.short: Collect service payments, record them, issue receipts and check daily totals.

steps.what: Find the service charge and confirm the amount due in the {ERP}.
Explain the charge and resolve questions before payment.
Take the authorised payment through the card-payment {OTHER}.
Record the successful payment against the service reference in the {ERP}.
Generate and give the customer a receipt.
Compare daily receipts with settlement totals and report discrepancies using the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure a service-reference checkout linking the {ERP} to the card-payment {OTHER}; the customer authorises the charge. A deterministic integration verifies successful payment events, prevents duplicate postings and triggers receipts from the {ERP}. A scheduled job in the {DATA_PLATFORM} matches postings to settlement data from the {BANK} and sends exceptions to the finance team.
tasks.previous_blocker: Payment acceptance was already electronic, but terminal results, service records and settlement reports were separate. Duplicate entry and reconciliation survived between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Payment references, supported event interfaces and existing receipt templates allow deterministic processing. AI-assisted coding makes the connecting and exception-handling code cheaper to produce.
tasks.still_hard: Cash, disputed charges, refunds, partial payments and settlement differences need separate handling. Reliable financial integration requires careful testing.
tasks.human_edge: The receptionist explains unexpected charges and helps customers with failed payments without making unauthorised concessions.

ambition.what: Same-day receipt correction support with finance-approved accounting changes.

tasks.altitude: Routine collection and entry largely disappear from the receptionist's week. The receptionist handles payment difficulties and receipt queries; refund and accounting adjustment rights do not change.

reach.task: Resolve payment-status and receipt enquiries.
reach.learn: Payment states, settlement timing and escalation to the finance team.

reach.task: Investigate recurring reception payment exceptions.
reach.learn: Reconciliation controls and separation of payment and adjustment permissions.

evidence.claim: Automatic charge routing exists in hospitality software; this is component evidence, not proof of this reception integration.
Reference matching, duplicate prevention and receipt generation are deterministic financial-processing patterns.
Structured payment work offers substantial automation despite the supplied human classification.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for an electronic-payment baseline.

assumptions: This task applies where reception collects service payments; many office receptions do not.
The baseline mainly uses card payments and a short daily reconciliation in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Amounts come from approved service charges, without discretionary pricing.
The customer approval gate concerns payment authorisation; remaining_pct measures staff time, not customer time.
Existing payment processing is retained; the integration does not store card credentials.
GDPR applies to payer details. Access approval and consultation under national rules are included where required.

Whether service references survive through payment and settlement.
Existing checkout, receipt and reconciliation capabilities.
Treatment of fees, refunds, deposits, tax and partial settlement.
Who may approve corrections and how financial controls are divided.

Do payment events support verified status, retries and duplicate prevention?
Can settlement differences be explained by explicit rules rather than free-text interpretation?
new_work: Review unmatched payments and settlement differences.
Handle failed payment events and integration retries.
Maintain charge mappings and receipt templates.
Check duplicate-prevention controls after interface changes.
Route corrections and refunds to authorised finance staff.
tasks.statement: Receive payment and record receipts for services.

tasks.short: Prepare, calculate and check administrative documents for the responsible team.

steps.what: Receive the request and collect its attachments.
Retrieve authorised records and check document versions.
Transcribe handwritten notes and document figures into the working table.

loop.input: Source pages and a fixed field schema.
loop.output: Staged fields linked to their source locations.
loop.check: Validate types, required fields and totals; a receptionist checks ambiguous handwriting and material figures.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per document; unresolved fields enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports handle digital records, but handwritten notes and variable layouts need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Calculate totals and compare them with the supporting records.
Proofread the draft and resolve discrepancies against the sources.

loop.input: Draft, source passages, calculation results and proofreading rules.
loop.output: Suggested corrections with source references and unresolved discrepancies.
loop.check: Protect amounts and identifiers with exact comparisons; the receptionist approves wording changes.
loop.stop: One checking pass and one revision; unsupported corrections remain flagged for a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch arithmetic and formatting errors; wording and transcription inconsistencies sometimes require contextual reading.

steps.what: Send the checked document and outstanding questions to the responsible team.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} collects requests from {EMAIL} and retrieves authorised records from {DOCS}, {ERP} or {PAYROLL}. Deterministic calculations and bounded extraction produce a checked draft, with human review of uncertain fields and wording. {WORKFLOW} routes the approved packet to its owner; financial posting and payroll approval remain separate actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable documents, handwriting and fragmented access made a single reliable intake difficult. Small administrative volumes often did not justify bespoke integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing capture and workflow capabilities cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building validators, templates and small connectors.
tasks.still_hard: Poor handwriting, conflicting originals and restricted payroll access remain costly. A receptionist cannot resolve accounting or payroll policy questions alone.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently minor discrepancies need the responsible team's attention and obtain missing context discreetly.

ambition.what: A daily administrative exception digest for team owners.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying figures to resolving incomplete requests and checking exceptions. The receptionist can prioritise the exception queue within an agreed remit; financial decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare consistent replies about missing administrative information.
reach.learn: Document templates, source referencing and clear exception descriptions.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of administrative rework.
reach.learn: Exception categories, turnaround measures and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Document capture can validate fields and route exceptions before writing to financial records; this supports the pattern, not universal handwriting accuracy.
Configured self-service and integration can reduce repeated entry into employee and payroll records.
Calculations, exact comparisons and document assembly can use deterministic code.

assumptions: This is delegated clerical preparation, not independent payroll processing or financial approval.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Build ranges cover one document family and a limited set of authorised records.
Access design includes GDPR data minimisation and retention; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which administrative documents reception actually handles.
Whether reception has legitimate access to the required financial or payroll fields.
The proportion of handwriting, repeat templates and unreadable scans.
The responsible approvers and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which recurring document family has enough volume to justify integration?
Can structured source data eliminate transcription before extraction is introduced?
Which fields require complete human verification because errors are financially material?
new_work: Review uncertain extracted fields and suggested corrections.
Resolve missing sources and conflicting document versions.
Maintain calculation rules, templates, permissions and connectors.
Check retention and remove unnecessary copies of confidential records.
tasks.statement: Perform administrative support tasks, such as proofreading, transcribing handwritten information, or operating calculators or computers to work with pay records, invoices, balance sheets, or other documents.

tasks.short: Welcome visitors, confirm their destination, arrange admission and direct or escort them.

steps.what: Welcome the visitor and establish their purpose and assistance needs.
Check the expected-visitor record in the visitor-management {OTHER}.
Notify the host that the visitor has arrived.
Confirm willingness to receive the visitor and any escort arrangements.
Apply admission rules and issue an authorised visitor badge.
Explain the route or escort the visitor to the agreed destination.

tasks.design: Configure expected-visitor matching in the visitor-management {OTHER}, using approved appointment fields from the {CALENDAR}. Arrival notifications and host acknowledgements flow through the {WORKFLOW} and {CHAT}; badge fields are prefilled after receptionist approval. The receptionist keeps the welcome, admission judgement and physical escort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visitor tools often handled registration but left host contact and appointment details disconnected. Human presence was essential, which obscured the smaller paperwork opportunity.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing visitor-management features can connect pre-registration, notifications and badge printing. Simple integration work is cheaper to build and maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected visitors, unavailable hosts, accessibility needs and situations requiring security judgement.
tasks.human_edge: A person notices confusion, welcomes visitors respectfully and adapts assistance to the situation.

ambition.what: Prearranged accessible arrivals with a confirmed route and named escort.

tasks.altitude: The desk spends less time searching and chasing hosts, leaving more attention for arrivals. No additional security decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Plan reception and escort coverage for busy arrival periods.
reach.learn: Arrival forecasting, accessible routes and escalation arrangements.

evidence.claim: Configured pre-registration, host notifications and badge prefilling are established visitor-management patterns.
The proposed design needs no model loop; identity and admission exceptions remain human decisions.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, including host effort.

assumptions: The baseline has a visitor-management {OTHER}; a paper-based site would need a different integration estimate.
Host acknowledgement is required for the baseline visit type.
The {CALENDAR} supplies visit metadata without exposing meeting contents.
Visitor matching uses booking references or confirmed details, without biometric recognition.
GDPR applies to visitor records; national rules determine any employee consultation requirement.
Receptionist time estimates exclude walking by a separate escort.
unknowns: Existing visitor-management capabilities and interfaces.
Admission rules, badge permissions and security escalation roles.
Which visits need host acknowledgement or an escort.
Accessible routes and available assistance.
Visitor retention periods and consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing configuration replace separate arrival messages and repeated visitor entry?
Can a host acknowledge arrival without revealing their detailed availability?
new_work: Correct unmatched or duplicate visitor records.
Maintain host contacts, route information and badge templates.
Handle unanswered arrival notifications.
Review retention settings and failed badge printing.
tasks.statement: Greet persons entering establishment, determine nature and purpose of visit, and direct or escort them to specific destinations.

tasks.short: Hear complaints, agree appropriate remedies and coordinate follow-through.

steps.what: Listen to the complaint, clarify the problem and establish the desired outcome.
Retrieve relevant case history and service commitments from the {HELPDESK} and {CRM}.
Assess the complaint against policy and choose a proposed remedy.

loop.input: Complaint account, retrieved context and approved remedy policy.
loop.output: A factual brief and policy-linked remedy options.
loop.check: Require source references; validate limits with code; the receptionist judges suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing evidence or conflicting policy goes to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can enforce remedy limits but cannot reliably connect every free-text complaint to relevant policy.

steps.what: Obtain approval for remedies beyond the receptionist's delegated authority.
Explain the remedy or escalation and agree the next action with the customer.
Record the agreement and assign follow-up in the {HELPDESK}.

loop.input: Receptionist's brief notes and the confirmed resolution agreement.
loop.output: Complaint record and proposed follow-up fields.
loop.check: Receptionist confirms facts and commitments; required fields and owner identifiers are validated.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; save manually if agreement or ownership remains unclear.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need concise synthesis; assignment and reminders use fixed rules.

tasks.design: A case view joins authorised history from the {HELPDESK} and {CRM}, with deterministic remedy limits and a bounded loop that prepares policy-linked options. People hear the complaint and decide the remedy; the {WORKFLOW} routes approval exceptions, and reviewed notes create follow-up tasks in the {HELPDESK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and paperwork were bundled with a conversation that depends on trust. Case history and policy were difficult to consult while listening.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared case view, configured approval routing and short draft-generation loops can remove preparation work without replacing the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible account can be incomplete or disputed. Fair remedies, distressed visitors and commitments involving other departments still require human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: De-escalating tension, recognising unfair treatment and negotiating a remedy the customer can accept.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on one recurring visitor access problem supported by complaint records.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends more of each case listening and resolving it, with less searching and typing. A supervisor can delegate a specific remedy band after reviewing outcomes; the tool itself grants no additional authority.

reach.task: Coordinate a complaint that crosses departments.
reach.learn: Case ownership, remedy limits and how to confirm that promised actions actually happened.

reach.task: Choose a service improvement from recurring complaints.
reach.learn: Root-cause analysis and how to distinguish repeated symptoms from a shared cause.

evidence.claim: A study of 5,179 support agents found 14% more issues resolved per hour with an assistant; this does not establish reception complaint outcomes.
Zendesk supports customer-question handling with integrated records and actions.
Complaint listening and remedy negotiation require context and interpersonal judgement.

assumptions: The representative complaint starts at the desk; telephone and written complaints use equivalent handoffs.
Approval effort is averaged across complaints, including those that need no supervisor.
The design uses brief human notes rather than routine recording or emotion analysis.
EU GDPR applies; employee consultation and monitoring requirements depend on national rules.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: Which remedies receptionists may authorise and which role approves exceptions.
Whether customer identities can be matched safely across the {CRM} and {HELPDESK}.
How follow-up ownership and resolution are currently tracked.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which complaint categories benefit from preparation assistance without delaying the conversation?
How should a pilot measure accepted remedies, repeat contacts and unsupported draft claims?
new_work: Review draft case notes and policy-linked options.
Resolve missing identities, conflicting records and unassigned follow-up.
Maintain remedy limits, escalation routes and policy references.
Sample records for inaccurate commitments and unnecessary personal detail.
tasks.statement: Hear and resolve complaints from customers or the public.

tasks.short: File reception records, keep them accurate and manage their retention.

steps.what: Collect documents and attachments that need filing.
Identify the record category, case reference and access restrictions.

loop.input: Documents without reliable metadata and the approved filing taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed category and case reference, with supporting text.
loop.check: Validate categories and references against allowed values; never infer broader access permissions.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair attempt; ambiguous documents enter a restricted review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Source metadata and fixed rules handle structured records; miscellaneous correspondence lacks dependable identifiers.

steps.what: Copy document details into a separate reception filing register in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Save documents and metadata in the correct location in the {DOCS}.
Review duplicates, corrections and records due for retention action.

tasks.design: Configured capture writes source documents and validated metadata into the {DOCS}, whose search and views replace the separate {SPREADSHEET} register. Deterministic rules handle known document types, a bounded classification loop proposes metadata for exceptions, and the {WORKFLOW} routes uncertain records and retention actions for review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing conventions lived in people's habits, and a separate register compensated for weak search. Mixed correspondence lacked consistent metadata.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document libraries provide metadata, permissions, versioning and retention features. Small integrations and bounded classification can connect incoming material to those features.
tasks.still_hard: Historic duplicates, uncertain ownership and inconsistent retention rules require cleanup. A document's text alone cannot establish its correct access permissions or legal retention period.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising records whose context, sensitivity or continuing business value makes routine classification unsafe.

ambition.what: Temporary reception cover staff receive a searchable, permission-limited reception record view.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist handles a short exception queue instead of repeated copying and folder navigation. They can correct routine metadata within an agreed scope; access policy and disposal decisions stay with the records administrator.

reach.task: Diagnose failed document capture or missing access.
reach.learn: Permission inheritance, connector logs and how to reproduce a failed capture.

reach.task: Arrange reliable reception cover.
reach.learn: Which records cover staff need and how to test their access without exposing unrelated information.

evidence.claim: Configured document libraries can maintain metadata, versions, permissions and retention workflows.
AFAS demonstrates structured self-service changes flowing into downstream employee records; this is adjacent evidence for write-once records.
Rossum supports document capture, validation and exception routing; reception filing needs its own taxonomy and checks.

assumptions: The representative desk keeps a small separate register alongside the {DOCS}; this is not universal.
Physical originals are retained where required; scanning does not automatically permit disposal.
EU GDPR requires appropriate access, data minimisation and justified retention.
Employee consultation follows national rules where the change introduces relevant monitoring.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: Whether a separate register exists and what unique information it holds.
Which record categories, retention schedules and legal holds apply.
Whether the {DOCS} supports the required metadata and retention controls.
How much historic material needs migration or physical handling.
Who may approve disposal and access changes.
research_questions: Which existing {DOCS} features can replace the register without a custom records application?
Which incoming document types can be classified entirely from trustworthy source metadata?
new_work: Review ambiguous categories and missing case references.
Maintain filing rules and mappings when document types change.
Monitor failed captures, duplicates and permission exceptions.
Approve retention actions and verify that legal holds prevent disposal.

tasks.short: Send requested information and documents to customers through the appropriate channel.

steps.what: Read the request and identify the recipient, requested documents and delivery channel.

loop.input: Information request and approved document catalogue.
loop.output: Requested document identifiers, recipient and delivery channel.
loop.check: Validate identifiers against the catalogue; preserve the supplied address without guessing.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; route missing or ambiguous details to the receptionist.
loop.why_not_simpler: A structured request form handles new requests; existing free-text requests still need interpretation.

steps.what: Find the current approved documents in the {DOCS}.
Prepare the covering message and document bundle.
Check recipient details, document versions and disclosure permissions.
Send the documents through {EMAIL}, or arrange the requested physical delivery.
Record dispatch and follow up failed deliveries.

tasks.design: A request form in the {WORKFLOW} selects approved versions from the {DOCS} and generates a delivery bundle; a bounded extraction loop handles free-text requests from the {EMAIL}. Deterministic checks flag recipient and disclosure problems, the receptionist approves dispatch, and the {HELPDESK} records delivery failures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document versions, recipient details and dispatch records sit in separate places. Small volumes made bespoke integration difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, document metadata and delivery connectors cover most of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them; free-text extraction needs only a small bounded loop.
tasks.still_hard: Restricted documents need reliable recipient verification. Postal and fax destinations, missing permissions and inaccessible files still create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a technically correct bundle would confuse the recipient, disclose too much or fail their accessibility needs.

ambition.what: Accessible pre-visit information packs tailored to the visitor's stated needs.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time finding attachments and recording dispatch. They can assemble approved information packs, while document owners retain publication and disclosure authority.

reach.task: Prepare accessible standard correspondence.
reach.learn: Document accessibility, approved templates and channel-specific delivery requirements.

evidence.claim: Template assembly, version selection and dispatch logging can use deterministic rules.
TOPdesk Robin can turn an unanswered knowledge request into a pre-filled request.
Rossum demonstrates document extraction with validation and exception routing; this is adjacent evidence, not a reception dispatch case.

assumptions: Most requests concern existing approved documents, rather than newly authored advice.
The representative route is electronic; physical delivery remains an exception.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured results.
EU GDPR applies to recipient data and document disclosure.
unknowns: Whether approved versions and disclosure categories are maintained in the {DOCS}.
Which delivery channels remain mandatory and how often physical handling occurs.
Whether the receptionist has authority to release each document category.
Which connectors and service accounts are available.
research_questions: Which existing {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} configuration covers version selection and dispatch without custom code?
Which delivery methods provide accessible files and usable failure notifications?
new_work: Review extracted request details and flagged disclosure issues.
Maintain document mappings and covering-message templates.
Resolve failed deliveries and connector failures.
Check that withdrawn documents cannot enter new delivery bundles.
tasks.statement: Transmit information or documents to customers, using computer, mail, or facsimile machine.

tasks.short: Arrange appointments, resolve scheduling conflicts and keep calendars current.

steps.what: Read the appointment request and collect missing booking requirements.
Check employee availability, appointment duration and any room constraints in the {CALENDAR}.
Send suggested times and chase a reply.
Agree a suitable time and resolve clashes or unusual requirements.
Create or update the appointment and reserve required resources in the {CALENDAR}.
Send confirmation, directions and any later appointment changes.

tasks.design: Configure a booking form and live availability in the {CALENDAR}, with explicit duration, resource, buffer and cancellation rules. Customers select permitted slots directly, removing proposal-and-chase messages; confirmations and changes use the {EMAIL}. The {WORKFLOW} routes conflicts and requests outside the rules to the receptionist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared calendars showed availability but did not always expose safe bookable slots. Incomplete requests and informal exceptions kept the receptionist in the middle.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured booking forms, availability checks and notifications handle the main flow without a model. Small deterministic connectors can cover resource rules missing from existing configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, calendars that do not reflect real availability and appointments requiring special arrangements.
tasks.human_edge: The receptionist negotiates workable alternatives when a valid request does not fit the published slots.

ambition.what: An opt-in cancellation waitlist for customers seeking an earlier appointment.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist mainly handles exceptions and helps people who cannot use self-service. Within delegated booking rules, they can offer alternative resources or times; overriding another employee's commitments still needs permission.

reach.task: Manage cancellations and short-notice availability.
reach.learn: Capacity rules, waitlist ordering and expiring slot offers.

reach.task: Adjust appointment capacity to recurring demand.
reach.learn: Aggregate demand analysis and resource scheduling.

evidence.claim: Structured appointment booking, availability checks and confirmations can usually be configured without model reasoning.
Direct slot selection removes proposal-and-chase work rather than merely drafting it faster.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges assume routine office or service appointments.

assumptions: Appointment types have stable durations and explicit booking permissions.
The baseline uses the {CALENDAR}, with requests and time proposals passing through the {EMAIL}.
After the change, customer slot selection supplies the agreed appointment; staff handle exceptions only.
People without suitable digital access retain a receptionist-assisted route.
No model reads appointment reasons or assigns priority.
GDPR applies to appointment details. National rules govern consultation where employee availability or working arrangements are affected.
A cancellation waitlist would use opt-in participation and explicit ordering rules.

Whether room and employee availability are reliable.
Actual exception rates and assisted-booking needs.
Permitted delegation, retention settings and consultation requirements under national rules.

Does booking recheck availability before committing and prevent simultaneous reservations?

Handle conflicts and assisted bookings.
Check failed confirmations and calendar synchronisation.
Review aggregate unused capacity and booking exceptions.
Maintain waitlist consent and ordering if the new service is introduced.
tasks.statement: Schedule appointments and maintain and update appointment calendars.

tasks.short: Find and interpret information to answer customer and public inquiries.

steps.what: Clarify the question, relevant circumstances and any identity requirement.
Look up relevant guidance, service records and current operational information.
Compare dates, figures and service conditions to establish the factual answer.
Interpret guidance and decide whether the answer needs specialist confirmation.

loop.input: Clarified question, authorised source passages, calculated facts and escalation rules.
loop.output: A short answer brief with citations, uncertainty and a proposed escalation reason.
loop.check: Check citations and source dates; compare figures exactly; a receptionist approves interpretation within their remit.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing, conflicting or restricted sources trigger specialist handoff.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed lookups answer standard questions, but unfamiliar wording and contextual explanations need bounded reading and drafting.

steps.what: Explain the answer, check understanding and agree the next action.
Record the outcome and route unresolved questions to the appropriate team.

loop.input: Approved answer brief and the receptionist's short outcome note.
loop.output: A proposed inquiry record and structured specialist request.
loop.check: Require valid categories, preserve agreed actions and let the receptionist check the summary before saving.
loop.stop: One drafting pass; incomplete records return to the receptionist for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed fields handle routing, but summarising a free-text outcome note needs a bounded drafting step.

tasks.design: An internal answer desk retrieves permitted information from {HELPDESK}, {CRM} and {DOCS}, using fixed queries and deterministic calculations for factual results. A bounded model drafts cited explanations for receptionist review, while {WORKFLOW} prepares records and specialist handoffs in {HELPDESK}. Logged source conflicts feed a small {BI} view for prioritising information corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers were spread across records, guidance and staff knowledge. Search alone did not reconcile stale guidance with current service data.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintained knowledge sources, controlled queries and bounded drafting can assemble useful answer briefs. AI-assisted coding makes the small retrieval and validation components cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies, unclear disclosure rights and unusual circumstances still require people. Integration quality and source ownership matter more than fluent wording.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the person actually needs, recognise distress or confusion and explain limits without making unsupported promises.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of corrections to reception service information.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time searching and calculating, and more time explaining answers and resolving ambiguity. Within an agreed remit, they can prioritise knowledge corrections; service owners retain policy decisions.

reach.task: Resolve inquiries that require service-history interpretation.
reach.learn: Case ownership, disclosure boundaries and service escalation rules.

reach.task: Diagnose missing knowledge and failed information retrieval.
reach.learn: Source provenance, access failures and reproducible issue reports.

Fixed calculations and permission-filtered record queries can remain deterministic.

How often do current sources conflict or lack an owner?

new_work: Maintain approved sources, query mappings and calculation rules.
Review uncertain answer briefs and specialist handoffs.
Correct stale guidance and investigate source conflicts.
Sample answer accuracy and access-control behaviour.
Maintain the evaluation set as services and policies change.
tasks.statement: Analyze data to determine answers to questions from customers or members of the public.

tasks.short: Explain where people and departments are located and what services the organisation provides.

steps.what: Ask what the visitor needs and clarify the destination or service.
Look up approved department locations, contact routes and service descriptions in the {DOCS}.
Confirm unclear or outdated information with the relevant department through {CHAT}.
Explain the service or route, adapting the answer to the visitor's needs.

loop.input: Visitor question and current, public-approved directory or service entries.
loop.output: A plain-language answer with source references and approved directions.
loop.check: Allow only current public sources; check destinations and links; disclose automated assistance.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one answer attempt; unsupported, ambiguous or access-sensitive questions go to reception.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search and fixed route cards handle common questions; varied wording and service explanations need bounded synthesis.

steps.what: Contact the host when the visitor needs an escort or further assistance.

tasks.design: A public directory and service catalogue in the {DOCS} feed searchable pages in the {CMS}, with fixed route cards for common destinations. A bounded answer loop handles varied questions using only approved public entries and hands uncertain cases to reception; the {WORKFLOW} routes stale entries and host notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information changed across departments without a reliable public directory. Receptionists supplied the missing context and knew which internal details should remain private.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured directories, content ownership and existing search cover most inquiries. A small grounded answer loop can explain approved information without accessing the whole employee directory.
tasks.still_hard: Live availability, temporary building changes and visitors who need personal assistance remain difficult. Internal employee records must not become a public search index.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing confusion, mobility or language needs and arranging a respectful handoff when directions alone are insufficient.

ambition.what: An after-hours public wayfinding and service-information desk on the {CMS}.

tasks.altitude: Routine questions shift to self-service, leaving the receptionist more time for visitors who need help. They can flag and propose directory corrections; department owners approve substantive service changes.

reach.task: Maintain answers to recurring public service questions.
reach.learn: Knowledge article structure, source ownership and accessible plain-language explanations.

reach.task: Route callers using the same approved contact directory.
reach.learn: Department routing, fallback contacts and which contact details may be disclosed.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base and creates a pre-filled request when it cannot answer.
Anglia Ruskin University reportedly handled 75% of chats with TOPdesk; this vendor case does not establish reception-wide savings.
Zendesk offers automated answers across chat, email and voice.
Public directories and fixed route cards can answer common location questions without a model.

assumptions: A useful share of inquiries concerns stable, public information.
Remaining human time reflects some routine inquiries moving to self-service; personal assistance remains available.
EU GDPR applies to directory data, and automated conversations must meet applicable EU AI Act disclosure requirements.
National rules determine any employee consultation needed for directory publication or changed work practices.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: Which employee details, locations and contact routes are approved for public disclosure.
Whether each department has an accountable directory and service-content owner.
Which languages, accessibility needs and after-hours channels visitors require.
How often questions involve security-sensitive areas or live availability.
Whether a public directory already exists.
research_questions: What proportion of common inquiries can fixed search results and route cards resolve?
Which accessibility checks and fallback routes are needed for unattended use?
How can source freshness and unsupported answers be tested before launch?
new_work: Maintain public directory entries, maps and service descriptions.
Review unanswered questions and unsupported answer samples.
Handle stale-source alerts and temporary route changes.
Test accessibility, language quality and handoff availability.
tasks.statement: Provide information about establishment, such as location of departments or offices, employees within the organization, or services provided.

tasks.short: Maintain staff availability so reception can route enquiries and visitors.

steps.what: Receive staff availability changes through the {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Check shared calendars for absences, meetings and expected return times.
Copy staff status and return times into the shared {SPREADSHEET} register.
Call staff or their team to clarify missing or conflicting availability.
Share the updated availability register with reception cover through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A restricted view in the {WORKFLOW} combines the staff directory from the {HCM}, free/busy information from the {CALENDAR} and staff-entered contact status. It replaces the copied register, expires temporary updates and flags conflicting information for reception. Show contactability and an authorised backup contact, without medical reasons, meeting titles or continuous location tracking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Calendar entries, staff messages and the reception register had different owners and no agreed freshness rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendar permissions and simple status forms provide most of the components. A small deterministic integration can join them without interpreting messages or inferring whereabouts.
tasks.still_hard: A free calendar does not prove someone is reachable. Staff must correct status, and access must respect GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Handle urgent contact requests discreetly and establish a reliable alternative when recorded availability is wrong.

ambition.what: Choose an authorised backup contact whenever the requested employee is unavailable.

tasks.altitude: Daily copying largely disappears, leaving a short queue of stale or disputed statuses. The receptionist gains a proposed mandate to select from approved backup contacts; staffing decisions remain with the office supervisor.

reach.task: Route unanswered calls to a suitable backup contact.
reach.learn: Use contact permissions, status expiry and escalation routes without disclosing private whereabouts.

evidence.claim: Staff-entered status, calendar free/busy and expiry rules can support a deterministic reception view.
AFAS supports employee self-service record changes; this supports the input pattern, not the complete availability design.
GDPR requires purpose limitation, data minimisation and appropriate access controls for staff information.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages require local validation.

assumptions: A shared {SPREADSHEET} currently bridges staff messages and calendars; some companies already have a suitable directory.
Calendar access exposes free/busy information rather than private event details.
Staff updates replace existing messages; employee effort is not assumed to disappear.
Access estimates include GDPR assessment and employee or works-council consultation under national rules where applicable; elapsed waiting may be longer.
unknowns: Which staff status fields reception is authorised to see.
Whether current calendar permissions allow free/busy integration.
Who supplies backup contacts and resolves contradictory status.
Which national consultation requirements and existing agreements apply.
research_questions: Which calendar states reliably indicate contactability without exposing event details?
What retention and consultation requirements apply to the proposed status view under national rules?
new_work: Resolve stale or conflicting status records.
Maintain backup contacts and access groups.
Review temporary-status expiry rules.
Explain the status process to staff and reception cover.
tasks.statement: Keep a current record of staff members' whereabouts and availability.

tasks.short: Receive, route and hand over incoming mail and parcels, and prepare outgoing deliveries.

steps.what: Receive deliveries and check visible damage, addressees and delivery paperwork.
Sort letters, parcels and messages by recipient, department and handling restrictions.
Enter tracked deliveries and storage locations in the reception log.
Notify recipients about deliveries and pass on messages.
Hand over items to recipients and record collection where required.
Package outgoing items and check the supplied address and dispatch instructions.
Book the courier, print the label and arrange collection.

tasks.design: Configure a delivery register in {WORKFLOW}, using a permitted directory from {HCM} and collection notices through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. Structured dispatch requests generate labels and prepare bookings through {PARTNER_PORTAL}, with approval before a chargeable booking. Physical receipt, sorting, packaging and handover remain with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling dominates the task. Separate logs, directory lookups and courier entry added small amounts of administration that were easy to overlook.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, barcode input and notifications can remove repeated entry. Small deterministic connectors can prepare courier bookings where interfaces permit.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear addressees, damaged parcels, restricted deliveries and secure custody require local judgement. Integration does not move physical items.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damage, protect confidential items and arrange a dependable handover when the intended recipient is unavailable.

ambition.what: Self-service parcel collection status for employees.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time typing notices and answering collection-status questions. The physical workload remains substantial, and dispatch spending authority does not change.

reach.task: Plan storage and collection arrangements around delivery peaks.
reach.learn: Queue age, storage capacity and escalation for uncollected items.

reach.task: Route messages using a shared recipient directory.
reach.learn: Directory ownership, absence routing and confidential message handling.

evidence.claim: A structured register, directory lookup and event-triggered notices need no model loop.
Software can reduce delivery administration while physical sorting and custody remain manual.

assumptions: A basic delivery log in {SPREADSHEET} is a representative setup, not universal practice.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Courier integration covers one provider interface and ordinary domestic shipments.
Messages already received electronically enter the same routing queue without being retyped.
Directory access and delivery-log retention follow GDPR; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Delivery volumes, sites and current logging tools.
Whether the courier interface permits booking integration.
Which items require signatures, identity checks or restricted storage.
Whether employees may collect parcels without reception staff present.
Whether the proposed register changes employee monitoring arrangements under national rules.
research_questions: Can electronic invoices and routine correspondence bypass reception entirely?
Which notifications and duplicate log entries can be removed?
Does barcode capture save enough time at the site's actual parcel volume?
new_work: Maintain recipient and deputy mappings.
Resolve unmatched recipients and failed notices.
Check booking failures and duplicate shipments.
Remove expired delivery records and review uncollected items.
tasks.statement: Collect, sort, distribute, or prepare mail, messages, or courier deliveries.

tasks.short: Calculate service prices and give customers accurate quotes.

steps.what: Ask which service, date, quantity and customer category the customer needs.
Find the current tariff and applicable conditions in the {DOCS}.
Calculate the price, taxes and permitted discounts in the {CRM} quote screen.
Approve exceptional discounts or unclear conditions before releasing a nonstandard quote.
Explain the quote and its validity to the customer.

tasks.design: Configure the {CRM} quote calculator with versioned tariffs, required fields and permitted discounts; link its conditions to the {DOCS}. A form in the {WORKFLOW} offers standard quotes outside reception hours, while exceptional prices require a service manager's approval before release. Receptionists retain conversations about unclear needs and conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tariffs and conditions were maintained separately, and exception handling made a small calculator project seem larger.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing quote features often cover the arithmetic. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting tariff versions, forms and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping prices current, interpreting unusual requests and handling regulated products remain costly.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when the customer has misunderstood the service and explain commitments before they accept.

ambition.what: After-hours self-service quotes for standard services.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time finding tariffs and calculating totals. They can issue standard quotes within an agreed price mandate; exceptional pricing remains with the service manager.

reach.task: Resolve disputed quotes.
reach.learn: Read tariff versions, explain exclusions and recognise when a quote needs escalation.

evidence.claim: Published tariffs, taxes and fixed discounts can be calculated deterministically.
Rossum supports price-rule checks and exception routing in order workflows; this is adjacent capability.
The proposed effort and remaining-time percentages are estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The representative case is quoting ordinary company services, rather than investment or insurance advice.
The {CRM} has configurable quote calculations; otherwise a deterministic calculator is needed.
The exception step's share is averaged across standard and exceptional enquiries.
Build estimates cover one tariff family and include access checks and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Where approved tariffs, taxes and discount limits are maintained.
Whether the {CRM} can calculate and version quotes.
Which quotes receptionists may release without further approval.
How frequently customers need advice rather than a price.
research_questions: Which regulated services require additional quote disclosures or qualified advice?
Can configured quote features reproduce historical prices and validity conditions?
new_work: Maintain tariff versions and effective dates.
Review failed calculations and nonstandard requests.
Test price changes before publication.
Monitor expired quotes and failed connections.
tasks.statement: Calculate and quote rates for tours, stocks, insurance policies, or other products or services.

tasks.short: Capture merchandise or material orders and route them to the department responsible for fulfilment.

steps.what: Receive the request and establish the requester, items, quantities and delivery needs.
Enter request details into a draft order in the {ERP}.

loop.input: Free-text order details or attached order document; structured requests bypass the model.
loop.output: Draft order fields with source references and unresolved item candidates.
loop.check: Validate schema, required fields, requester identity, units and item identifiers against master data; show uncertain fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per request; unresolved fields go to the receptionist without posting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms handle standard requests, but variable descriptions and documents need extraction. A bounded call is sufficient.

steps.what: Check item codes, quantities, availability, prices and delivery details.
Clarify ambiguous items, unavailable stock or unusual delivery needs with the requester.
Approve the order for fulfilment, including any agreed exceptions.
Send the released order to the responsible department and record the handoff.

tasks.design: Use a structured form in the {WORKFLOW} to create draft orders in the {ERP}; a bounded extraction loop prepares drafts from free text and documents for review. Configure master-data checks and an approval queue in the {ERP}, then route released orders to department queues with a recorded handoff. Receptionists handle clarification with the validation result already prepared.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requesters use inconsistent descriptions, and reception lacks a reliable bridge between incoming requests, item records and department routing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing order validation and routing can handle the fixed rules. Bounded extraction handles variable documents, while AI-assisted coding can shorten integration work.
tasks.still_hard: Poor item data, ambiguous units, stock timing and substitution agreements remain difficult. Routing a request does not establish that fulfilment has accepted it.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the requester actually needs and negotiate practical alternatives when stock or delivery constraints conflict.

ambition.what: A reception order status service showing which department accepted the request and its next update.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time entering and forwarding orders and more time resolving unclear requests and stalled handoffs. Commercial exceptions and release authority remain with the fulfilment coordinator.

reach.task: Resolve order-status and substitution inquiries.
reach.learn: Order states, item alternatives and limits on delivery commitments.

reach.task: Triage failures between request intake and order creation.
reach.learn: Validation errors, access permissions and duplicate-safe retry procedures.

evidence.claim: Email and document order capture can check customer, stock and price rules, route exceptions and post into finance systems.
A vendor case reports 70% touchless orders at allnex; this does not establish a reception-specific saving.
Structured order imports and stock synchronisation are established capabilities.
Department routing, duplicate checks and release gates can use deterministic rules.

assumptions: These are customer orders handled at reception, rather than internal purchasing requisitions.
The {ERP} contains usable item, stock and price records.
Clarification is conditional; its share represents average time across all orders.
A fulfilment coordinator currently approves release, and that decision right is retained.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one intake route and one {ERP} connection with existing interfaces.
Access work includes GDPR data handling and employee consultation where national rules require it; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Whether orders are customer sales, internal material requests or a mixture.
Request volumes, channels, document formats and item ambiguity.
Available {ERP} interfaces, licences and approval features.
Who may approve substitutions, discounts and delivery commitments.
How departments acknowledge requests and report fulfilment progress.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: How much intake can move to structured fields without increasing requester effort?
Which validation and routing features already exist in the {ERP}?
Can every extracted item and unit be traced to the original request?
How will retries avoid duplicate orders and duplicate fulfilment requests?
Which failures require clarification before release?
new_work: Review extracted drafts and unresolved item matches.
Maintain item aliases, validation rules and department routing.
Handle failed transfers, duplicate warnings and unacknowledged handoffs.
Sample extraction quality after document or catalogue changes.
Maintain access permissions and order-data retention.
tasks.statement: Take orders for merchandise or materials and send them to the proper departments to be filled.

tasks.short: Prepare correspondence and administrative documents, including travel vouchers.

steps.what: Receive document requests and supporting details through the {EMAIL}.
Find the approved template, source facts and policy in the {DOCS}.
Draft the memo or correspondence using the approved template in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved template, request fields and a permission-filtered document source pack.
loop.output: Correspondence draft with source references and explicit missing-information flags.
loop.check: Validate required fields, recipients, dates and amounts against source data; require human approval before sending.
loop.stop: At most two drafting attempts and 60 seconds; unresolved facts return to the receptionist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed text uses template merging; variable explanations require writing from supplied facts.

steps.what: Enter travel details and attach receipts to a voucher in the {EXPENSE}.
Check the correspondence's facts, tone and recipients before approving it.
Approve or return the travel voucher under the expense policy.
Send the approved correspondence through the {EMAIL}.
File the final correspondence and its reference in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Forms in the {WORKFLOW} collect required facts and select approved templates from the {DOCS}; fixed correspondence uses field merging, with a bounded drafting loop only for variable prose. Structured travel details and attached receipts populate the {EXPENSE}, where the budget holder retains approval. Correspondence approval unlocks sending through the {EMAIL} and automatic filing in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived with missing details, templates drifted and free-form writing made the whole process appear unsuitable for automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms and templates handle the stable parts. Bounded drafting can now handle variable prose, while inexpensive integration connects approval, sending and filing.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive wording, incomplete evidence and unusual expenses still need judgement. Source references and field checks cannot guarantee that every drafted statement is correct.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when wording could harm a relationship, reveal private information or imply an unauthorised commitment.
tasks.altitude: The receptionist reviews prepared drafts and handles incomplete or sensitive requests instead of retyping standard documents. Approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare and quality-check customer correspondence.
reach.learn: Control template versions, verify source facts and edit tone for the recipient.

reach.task: Resolve recurring administrative exceptions.
reach.learn: Distinguish missing information, policy exceptions and requests requiring a qualified approver.

evidence.claim: Template merging, structured intake, approval routing and filing can be deterministic.
Variable correspondence can be drafted from a case record, with a person approving release.
Preparation automation does not establish whether an expense should be authorised.
The proposed effort and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates.

assumptions: The steps show correspondence and travel-voucher branches; not every request follows both branches.
Time shares are averaged across the document mix.
Travel details are supplied through structured fields; receipt attachments remain available to the approver.
The {EXPENSE} supports structured draft creation; otherwise deterministic integration adds effort.
Build ranges cover a small template set and include access, privacy checks and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which document types dominate the workload.
Which templates and policies are approved and current.
Who may approve sensitive correspondence.
Whether the {EXPENSE} accepts structured imports or draft records.
Which data may be processed by the drafting service under existing agreements.
research_questions: Which document types can use fixed field merging without a model?
How can the drafting service enforce source permissions and retention requirements?
Which validation methods best detect unsupported statements in this document mix?
new_work: Review variable drafts and missing-information flags.
Maintain templates, source permissions and policy versions.
Handle returned vouchers and failed deliveries.
Sample approved correspondence for factual and privacy errors.
Maintain drafting instructions and checks when document types change.
tasks.statement: Process and prepare memos, correspondence, travel vouchers, or other documents.

tasks.short: Book programme space and equipment, and prepare participant lists.

steps.what: Read the organiser's request for dates, capacity, equipment and attendees.
Check room capacity and availability in the {CALENDAR}.
Check equipment availability and setup times in the shared {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree alternatives with the organiser when timing, access or resource requirements conflict.
Reserve the room and setup interval in the {CALENDAR}.
Record the equipment reservation in the shared {SPREADSHEET}.
Combine registrations and organiser updates into a participant list in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Send booking confirmations and the appropriate participant information through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A form in the {WORKFLOW} checks required details and uses the {CALENDAR} for rooms and bookable equipment, replacing the equipment {SPREADSHEET}. Deterministic checks enforce capacity, setup intervals and resource availability; failed partial reservations are released before confirmation. Registration records generate restricted participant lists and confirmations through the {EMAIL}, while organisers approve changes to their requirements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rooms, equipment and registrations were tracked separately, making cancellations and partial bookings awkward to coordinate.
tasks.enabler_now: Resource-calendar configuration covers ordinary bookings. Small integrations can handle setup intervals, registration lists and failed reservation recovery.
tasks.still_hard: Competing priorities, accessibility needs and late changes require discussion. Software cannot establish whether equipment is physically ready.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate workable alternatives and notice practical needs that the organiser omitted.

ambition.what: Self-service booking for small internal programmes with standard resource needs.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist handles resource conflicts and event readiness instead of copying reservations and names. A proposed remit lets them allocate equivalent standard resources within organiser-approved limits.

reach.task: Resolve booking conflicts and coordinate replacements.
reach.learn: Manage capacity, temporary holds, cancellation rules and confirmations.

reach.task: Prioritise scarce shared resources.
reach.learn: Assess competing programme needs and escalate priority disputes.

evidence.claim: Resource calendars and structured registrations can support deterministic booking and participant-list generation.
Cross-resource reservations require conflict checks and recovery from partial failure.
Effort and remaining-time estimates assume ordinary internal programmes rather than large public events.

assumptions: Rooms use the {CALENDAR}, while portable equipment and participant lists still use a {SPREADSHEET}.
Routine bookings proceed within the original request; only changed requirements need organiser approval.
Structured registration replaces manual consolidation; unusual updates remain exceptions.
Participant lists go only to authorised organisers; attendees do not receive other attendees' details by default.
Access estimates include privacy review and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether equipment can be configured as calendar resources.
Which bookings require facilities approval or payment.
How organisers define priority and acceptable substitutions.
Whether external participants or sensitive access requirements are involved.
research_questions: Can the configured resource calendar prevent conflicting bookings across all required resources?
Which reservation recovery method is available when one resource booking fails?
new_work: Maintain capacities, setup intervals and equipment availability.
Resolve failed partial bookings and cancellation exceptions.
Check physical readiness with the facilities coordinator.
Maintain recipient permissions and participant-list retention.
tasks.statement: Schedule space or equipment for special programs and prepare lists of participants.

tasks.short: Register people for programmes and notify them of acceptance.

steps.what: Collect applicant details and help complete the application form.
Check required fields, supporting documents and available places.
Decide admission and resolve eligibility, capacity or missing-document exceptions.
Copy accepted applicant details into the programme register.
Send acceptance details, joining instructions and any payment deadline.

tasks.design: Configure an accessible application form and programme register in the {WORKFLOW}, with criteria and joining instructions maintained in the {DOCS}. Required-field, document-presence and capacity checks prepare the coordinator's admission decision; approval changes the existing record to enrolled and triggers a template through the {EMAIL}. Keep assisted applications available at reception.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms, capacity lists and approval messages sit separately. Rekeying appears easier than agreeing one register and admission process.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, status rules and notifications can handle most steps. AI-assisted coding can shorten small integration work; no model is needed for the assumed checks.
tasks.still_hard: Document presence does not prove eligibility. Fair capacity allocation, unusual evidence and accessible assistance still require people.
tasks.human_edge: Explain requirements without discouraging applicants, recognise support needs and resolve admission exceptions fairly.

ambition.what: An applicant status service showing missing items and the next expected update.

tasks.altitude: The receptionist spends less time copying details and chasing updates, and more time helping applicants complete valid submissions. Admission rights remain with the programme coordinator.

reach.task: Resolve applicant questions about incomplete submissions.
reach.learn: Programme criteria, accessible explanations and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Review application delays and reception coverage.
reach.learn: Queue ageing, capacity constraints and staffing trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Configured self-service and record workflows are established capabilities; programme admission still needs its own rules.
Required-field checks, capacity rules and template notices can use deterministic workflows.
Solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects require assessment under GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: The programme is an ordinary customer or community programme, not statutory benefits, recruitment or credit.
Applications use defined fields and a finite document checklist.
Automated checks test completeness and capacity; a coordinator decides admission.
Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one programme, existing platform configuration and a small pilot; they are not measured delivery results.
The access range includes privacy review and any employee consultation required by national rules; formal consultation can take longer.
unknowns: Programme type, admission criteria and consequences of rejection.
Application volume, assisted-application demand and document formats.
Current register, available platform licences and access permissions.
Capacity allocation rules, retention periods and authorised approvers.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which checks establish completeness, and which require interpreting evidence?
Can the existing register support forms, approval states and notifications without custom code?
What happens when two approvals compete for the final place?
Which alternative channels do applicants need?
new_work: Maintain programme criteria, capacity limits and notice templates.
Handle incomplete applications and failed deliveries.
Review permissions, retention settings and admission logs.
Check that assisted applicants receive equivalent service.
tasks.statement: Enroll individuals to participate in programs and notify them of their acceptance.

tasks.short: Keep the reception area tidy, welcoming and ready for visitors.

steps.what: Inspect the lobby, plants, reading material and visitor seating.
Water plants, straighten reading material and restore the seating area.
Report faults, cleaning needs or missing supplies to the facilities team.

tasks.design: Keep inspection and physical care with the receptionist. Configure a short form in {HELPDESK} with location, issue category and an optional photo, so facilities requests route automatically and their status is visible.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work is physical and already simple. Automating plant care or tidying would usually cost more than it saves at a reception desk.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing {HELPDESK} forms can shorten issue reporting with little custom development. No model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Tidiness, plant condition and an accessible, welcoming layout require direct observation and physical action. Software cannot correct understaffing or slow facilities response.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what makes the space uncomfortable or difficult to use and adjust it sensitively while visitors are present.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little beyond less time composing and chasing facilities requests. No additional decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Coordinate recurring reception-area checks with facilities coverage.
reach.learn: Clear service ownership, accessible layouts and practical escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Configured request forms and routing can reduce facilities reporting effort; they do not automate physical care.

assumptions: Physical inspection and care dominate this task, despite the prior's high communication share.
The reporting share represents an average across days with and without facilities issues.
Build ranges assume an existing {HELPDESK} and no visitor or employee monitoring.
Photos avoid identifiable people; GDPR and applicable national consultation rules still apply.
unknowns: Whether reception or a facilities contractor owns plant care and tidying.
Actual time spent reporting and chasing issues.
Whether a suitable facilities request form already exists.
Which supplies and adjustments reception may authorise.
research_questions: Can a direct link to the existing facilities form solve the reporting problem without a build?
Would fewer loose materials or a simpler planting arrangement eliminate recurring care work?

Check stalled requests.
Occasionally review whether the form saves more time than it adds.
tasks.statement: Perform duties, such as taking care of plants or straightening magazines to maintain lobby or reception area.

Accessible communication and document preparation.
Knowledge-source maintenance and public disclosure boundaries.
Record classification, retention and permission basics.
Checking generated text against source records.
